modules.name: Overdrive
modules.description: Tube-screamer style mid push. Great in front of a high-gain amp.

modules.name: Ember Fuzz
modules.description: Thick, saturated fuzz with a mid-scoop tone control.

modules.name: Clean Boost
modules.description: Clean gain with a tight low cut. Pushes the amp without changing its character.

modules.name: Compressor
modules.description: Evens out your picking and adds sustain.

modules.name: Glue Compressor
modules.description: Smooth bus compressor that glues the whole rig together.

modules.name: Lament Wah
modules.description: Wah: set it by hand, let it sweep by itself (Auto) or follow your picking (Envelope).

modules.name: NAM Pedal
modules.description: Load a .nam capture of any drive, fuzz or boost pedal.

modules.name: Ascend Whammy
modules.description: Bends your guitar up or down. Sweep Position like an expression pedal.

modules.name: Abyss Octave
modules.description: Adds an octave below, two octaves below and an octave above.

modules.name: Richter Sub
modules.description: Earthquake sub-octave for huge low end.

modules.name: Photon Laser
modules.description: Every pick attack fires a falling resonant sweep: sci-fi lasers.

modules.name: Lethe Delay
modules.description: Digital, tape or ping-pong delay. Sync locks the repeats to the tempo.

modules.name: Crypt Reverb
modules.description: Deep, smooth room-to-cathedral reverb. Voice switches to the six Boss RV-6 modes (from the pedal pack).

modules.name: Seraph Shimmer
modules.description: Reverb whose tail rises an octave (or a fifth): angelic pads.

modules.name: Aurora Swell
modules.description: Removes the pick attack and swells each note in, violin-style, into a soft reverb.

modules.name: Stasis Freeze
modules.description: Hold the button to freeze the sound into an endless pad, then play over it.

modules.name: Gravity Tape Stop
modules.description: Hold to slow the sound down to a stop like a tape machine losing power.

modules.name: Looper
modules.description: Tap REC to record, tap again to play, again to overdub. Up to 60 seconds.

modules.name: Shatter Glitch
modules.description: Tempo-synced stutters, reverses and half-speed drops. Hold to glitch, or let Auto surprise you.

modules.name: Tide Chorus
modules.description: Lush stereo chorus, from subtle shimmer to thick 80s.

modules.name: Vortex Flanger
modules.description: Jet-plane flanger with feedback.

modules.name: Prism Phaser
modules.description: Swirling 4 to 12-stage phaser.

modules.name: Pulse Tremolo
modules.description: Volume tremolo: smooth, triangle or choppy square. Stereo mode pans it.

modules.name: Spectre Mod
modules.description: Vibrato, rotary speaker or uni-vibe.

modules.name: Tesla Ring Mod
modules.description: Metallic, bell-like ring modulation with a wobbling carrier.

modules.name: Hex Bitcrusher
modules.description: Lo-fi bit and sample-rate reduction.

modules.name: Bloom Envelope Filter
modules.description: Auto-wah that opens with your picking: funky quack to synth sweeps.

modules.name: Sweep Filter
modules.description: Resonant filter with an LFO, free or synced to the tempo.

modules.name: Limiter
modules.description: Catches peaks so nothing ever clips. Put it last.

modules.name: Chiron
modules.description: Transparent overdrive (Klon-style Centaur captures). Blend mixes your clean signal back in.

modules.name: Emperor
modules.description: Three-mode drive (Duke of Tone captures): boost, overdrive or distortion.

modules.name: Graven
modules.description: Tight metal overdrive (Fortin-modded TS-9 captures). Put it in front of a high-gain amp.

modules.name: Maw
modules.description: High-gain grinder (Fortin Grind captures).

modules.name: XXXIII
modules.description: Fortin 33 boost (Thordendal signature capture). Tightens and pushes the amp.

modules.name: Helios
modules.description: Super-overdrive (Boss SD-1 captures): three boost and six drive voices.

modules.name: Aeon
modules.description: Bass/guitar drive (Darkglass Alpha Omega Ultra captures): alpha or omega voice, Growl and Bite, seven drive steps.

modules.name: Ossuary
modules.description: Real catacomb reverb (Green-Wood Cemetery Catacombs IRs). Pick the room position and the mic.

modules.name: Halcyon
modules.description: Ambient shoegaze reverb (Tone Charm Audio IRs): a slap-back echo or a long percussive wash.

modules.name: Elysium Hall
modules.description: Huge, lush cathedral hall: early reflections, then a long, softly moving tail. INFINITE holds the tail forever while you play over it.

modules.name: Empyrean Shimmer
modules.description: Two-voice shimmer: an octave voice and a second interval rise through a lush tail, like a choir of strings.

modules.name: Nimbus Cloud
modules.description: Cloud reverb: notes dissolve into a slowly drifting haze. Swell fades the reverb in under each note; FREEZE holds the cloud.

modules.name: Vesper Choir
modules.description: Choir reverb: the tail sings through vowel formants (A E I O U). Voices adds an octave or a fifth; Breath makes the choir move.

modules.name: Halo Reverse
modules.description: REVERSE: every note's reverb plays backwards, swelling into the next. BLOOM: the tail comes back around and builds on itself.

modules.name: Astral Shimmer Delay
modules.description: Shimmer delay: each repeat climbs an octave (or a fifth) and can smear into a reverb-like wash with Diffuse.

modules.name: Mnemosyne Tape Echo
modules.description: Three-head tape echo with a spring reverb: pick the heads, age the tape, add wow. Intensity past 95% runs away like the real thing.

modules.name: Gemini Dual Delay
modules.description: Two delay heads in a rhythm (dotted, triplet, golden ratio...), cross-fed across the stereo field. REVERSE plays head B backwards.

modules.name: Lyra 12-String
modules.description: 12-string shimmer: adds a chiming octave string and a detuned twin to every note, strummed a hair apart.

modules.name: Icarus Octave Fuzz
modules.description: Octave-up fuzz: a searing fuzz with a ringing octave above it (best on the neck pickup, above the 7th fret).

amps.name: GLASS 65
amps.description: Huge, glassy clean with lots of headroom. Bright-cap sparkle at low gain, scooped Fender mids.

amps.name: TOP 30
amps.description: Chimey class-A breakup. No negative feedback, so the top end jangles and the power amp compresses early.

amps.name: PLEXI 68
amps.description: Classic rock crunch from a non-master amp: open and punchy, with more gain from the power tubes as you turn up.

amps.name: BRIT 800
amps.description: The 80s rock and metal workhorse: cascaded preamp, tight mids, cutting top. Great with a boost in front.

amps.name: SLO 100
amps.description: Smooth, liquid saturation with a vocal midrange. Sings on leads and still stays tight on rhythm.

amps.name: STYX 51
amps.description: Aggressive modern metal: very tight low end, saturated upper mids. Made for down-tuned riffs.

amps.name: RECTO
amps.description: Thick, saggy, dark modern gain with a big low end. The rectifier sag makes palm mutes bloom.

amps.name: VH-4
amps.description: Precise, articulate modern German gain: dense, but every note in a chord stays clear.

amps.name: OBSIDIAN CORE
amps.description: Obsidian's own amp: tight like a 5150, smooth like an SLO, with a clearer top end.

amps.name: Eidolon
amps.description: Load your own .nam captures (up to four) and step through them with PREV / NEXT or BROWSE.

face.name: Eidolon
face.intro: Eidolon is the NAM loader: a rack-style head with no capture of its own, for any capture you want to bring in. The screen stays simple and never moves around. The top half shows the slot number, the capture's name, the gear it was made from and whether it's amp only or full rig. The bottom row shows each knob's value, sitting right above that knob, and lights up the one you're turning.
notes: LOAD opens one or more .nam files from your phone or PC. The screen reads the name and gear info straight out of each file.
PREV and NEXT step back or forward one capture at a time. BROWSE is the fast way through a big list: turning it sweeps across all loaded captures, so a full turn goes from the first file to the last.
Gain, Bass, Middle, Treble, Presence and Master are the same tone stack every amp uses. In the plugin, Gain drives the input into whatever capture is loaded.
Files you open stay on your device. The page only reads the text inside them to show the name and gear info.
